issues.legal_issue: A homicide committed without premeditation during a sudden fight in the heat of passion, without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct, is culpable homicide rather than murder.
material_facts: The fatal assault followed a sudden quarrel arising from a long-running land dispute while a court-appointed commissioner was at the scene.
People on both sides sustained injuries, and one person on each side died a homicidal death.
The court found no clear evidence that either side took undue advantage or acted cruelly or unusually, and found no evidence of an intention to kill before the sudden confrontation.
The evidence established that the two appellants attacked the two deceased persons.
issues.conclusion: By majority, the court held that Exception 4 to section 300 of the Indian Penal Code applied to the two appellants who attacked the deceased. It altered their convictions from murder with common intention under sections 302/34 to culpable homicide under section 304(1)/34 and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for seven years.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to section 300 of the Indian Penal Code provides that culpable homicide is not murder when it is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offenders taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually. Applying those requirements to the sudden confrontation and the injuries and deaths on both sides, the majority applied section 304(1) read with section 34. No earlier cases are cited for this ruling.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and sudden_quarrel and heat_of_passion and no_premeditation and fatalities_on_both_sides and no_undue_advantage and no_cruel_or_unusual_conduct

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.sudden_quarrel: The fatal violence began during a sudden quarrel between the sides.
predicates.heat_of_passion: The participants acted in the heat of passion during the confrontation.
predicates.fatalities_on_both_sides: The confrontation resulted in a homicidal death on each side.
predicates.no_undue_advantage: The offenders did not take undue advantage during the fight.
predicates.no_cruel_or_unusual_conduct: The offenders did not act cruelly or unusually.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal concerns a homicide arising from an unpremeditated sudden quarrel in the heat of passion, with deaths on both sides and without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct, the murder conviction is reduced to culpable homicide.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction must be set aside when the evidence leaves reasonable doubt about whether an accused participated in the attacks or instigated them.
material_facts: The accused was about 70 years old at the time of the occurrence.
The court found reasonable doubt about whether he had caught hold of the injured man and whether he had directed his sons to attack and kill the deceased persons.
issues.conclusion: The court gave the accused the benefit of reasonable doubt, set aside his convictions under sections 302/34 and 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code, and acquitted him.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that an accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt. It found the evidence did not establish the accused's participation or instigation beyond reasonable doubt and acquitted him of the offences charged under sections 302/34 and 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code. No earlier cases are cited for this ruling.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_was_elderly: The accused was elderly at the time of the occurrence.
predicates.reasonable_doubt_about_participation: The evidence left reasonable doubt about whether the accused participated in or instigated the attacks.

issues.definition: When an elderly accused challenges a conviction and the evidence leaves reasonable doubt about that accused's participation, the conviction is set aside and the accused is acquitted.

issues.legal_issue: An attack with knives accompanied by the intention to commit murder, shared by the attackers, supports conviction for attempted murder with common intention even when the victim survives.
material_facts: The two appellants attacked an injured man with knives.
The court found that their intention was such that, had the victim died from the injuries, the attackers would have been guilty of murder in furtherance of their common intention.
The victim sustained multiple injuries, including a serious injury to the chest.
issues.conclusion: The court maintained the two appellants' convictions and sentences for attempted murder with common intention under sections 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, an attack with the intention or knowledge that would make the act murder if death resulted may constitute attempted murder even if the victim survives. Section 34 applies where the act is done in furtherance of the attackers' common intention. No earlier cases are cited for this ruling.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_conviction and coordinated_attack and attack_with_deadly_weapon and intent_sufficient_for_murder_if_death_resulted

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.coordinated_attack: The attackers acted together in carrying out the attack.
predicates.attack_with_deadly_weapon: The attackers used a weapon capable of causing death.
predicates.intent_sufficient_for_murder_if_death_re: The attackers had an intention that would make the act murder if the victim had died from the injuries.

issues.definition: When attackers act together, use a potentially deadly weapon, and have an intention sufficient for murder if death results, the attempted-murder conviction with common intention is maintained.
